guard: cotal_send still creates unknown channels, but the success receipt lets a caller tell a new name from a known one
why: Issue #989. A typo'd channel used to return the same success line as a send into a known
room. The discriminating assertion is that a caller can TELL, not that bogus send fails.
N1 restores the old identical success TEMPLATE (drop the receipt). The cell that
normalized success lines differ must redden. Raw strings still differ by channel name.
N2 makes closeChannelNames always empty, so a one-edit typo no longer names the match.
N3 makes every name look pre-existing, so the tool receipt never says new channel.
N5 makes the authed default the first concrete channel again: the live Cloud refusal on #announce.
N6 drops the refusal when no read channel is postable.
N7 sends the raw argument instead of the resolved default.
N8 drops the explicit channel check, so a pattern or a malformed name is described and handed to send.
N9 drops the first way to reach a family from the refusal.
N10 drops both ways from the advertised channel text.
N11 gives a name that breaks the channel grammar the pattern advice.
N12 drops the durable-backstop caveat from the refusal.
N13 lets a malformed name with no whole-segment wildcard through, so team.** is sent as team.__.
N14 shows a long name whole in the refusal instead of its first 64 characters.
N15 drops the channel grammar from the no-channel-name refusal.
N16 states a limit other than core's MAX_CHANNEL_LENGTH in the no-channel-name refusal.
N17 and N18 move the cut one character either way.
N19 cuts in the wrong place: the first 63 characters and then the last one.
NO BUILD STEP: the suite imports ../src.

mutations.name: N1 the success line ignores the receipt, restoring identical words for typo and known
mutations.expectRed: cotal_send on a typo says new channel so the caller can TELL
mutations.cell: cotal_send on a typo says new channel so the caller can TELL
mutations.note: The reported defect: success words no longer distinguish a typo from a known room.

mutations.name: N2 close matches are never suggested
mutations.replace: if (false && name !== channel && editDistanceAtMostOne(channel, name)) out.push(name);
mutations.expectRed: send to a one-edit typo reports new and names the close match
mutations.cell: send to a one-edit typo reports new and names the close match
mutations.note: Without close matches the caller can still see new but cannot see the likely intended name.

mutations.name: N3 describeSendChannel always reports existing, so a typo looks like a known room
mutations.expectRed: cotal_send on a typo says new channel so the caller can TELL
mutations.cell: cotal_send on a typo says new channel so the caller can TELL
mutations.note: If every name is 'existing', the tool receipt is identical to the old success line.

mutations.name: N4 #1229 assertKnownMentions refuses an absent name under a failed read with the old sentence
mutations.expectRed: 1229:e send under a failed read refuses naming the read's error and the missing grant, not "unknown mention"
mutations.cell: 1229:e send under a failed read refuses naming the read's error and the missing grant, not "unknown mention"
mutations.note: #1229: only a roster read that succeeded supports an absence verdict, so a mention of a live peer is not rejected because the read failed (an old credential without the Direct Get grant, a dropped link). Dropping the condition restores the reported defect: cell (e) sees the old 'unknown mention' refusal under a read that cannot support an absence verdict.

mutations.name: N5 the authed default is the first concrete channel read, restoring the refused #announce default
mutations.find: return isAuthed(config) ? concrete.find((c) => channelInAllow(config.allowPublish, c)) : concrete[0];
mutations.expectRed: an omitted channel goes to the first channel the agent may post to
mutations.cell: an omitted channel goes to the first channel the agent may post to
mutations.note: The live Cloud defect: an agent reading [announce, team.rocket] with post rights on team.rocket only sent to #announce and the broker refused it.

mutations.name: N6 no refusal before sending when the agent may post to none of the channels it reads
mutations.find: if (target === undefined && joined.some(isConcreteChannel)) return err(`Couldn't send: ${NO_POSTABLE_DEFAULT}.`);
mutations.expectRed: with no channel it may post to, an omitted channel is refused before sending
mutations.cell: with no channel it may post to, an omitted channel is refused before sending
mutations.note: Without the guard the send goes out with no channel, the endpoint picks the read-only one, and the broker refusal is the only signal.

mutations.name: N7 the resolved default is computed but the raw argument is sent, so the endpoint picks the read-only channel
mutations.find: const m = await agent.send(msg, target, mentions);
mutations.replace: const m = await agent.send(msg, channel, mentions);
mutations.expectRed: an omitted channel goes to the first channel the agent may post to
mutations.cell: an omitted channel goes to the first channel the agent may post to
mutations.note: The receipt would describe team.rocket while the message went to the endpoint default.

mutations.name: N8 an explicit channel is no longer checked before the send path
mutations.expectRed: cotal_send refuses the pattern team.> before reading or sending
mutations.cell: cotal_send refuses the pattern team.> before reading or sending
mutations.note: Without the guard a pattern or a malformed name reaches describeSendChannel, which reads the channel list, and then the endpoint, which refuses a whole-segment pattern without either way and rewrites a malformed name onto another subject.

mutations.name: N9 the refusal stops naming one post to a channel the pattern matches
mutations.find: To reach the agents connected and following ${channel} now, post once to one channel it matches.
mutations.expectRed: the refusal for team.> says one post to a channel it matches reaches its connected followers
mutations.cell: the refusal for team.> says one post to a channel it matches reaches its connected followers
mutations.note: The refusal would still refuse but would teach only the per-channel way.

mutations.name: N10 the advertised channel text drops both ways to reach a family
mutations.find: }). ${PATTERN_SEND_HELP} Reply on the channel you received a message on.`
mutations.replace: }). Reply on the channel you received a message on.`
mutations.expectRed: the advertised channel text names both ways to reach a family
mutations.cell: the advertised channel text names both ways to reach a family
mutations.note: An agent reading the tool schema would learn of the refusal only by hitting it.

mutations.name: N11 a name that breaks the channel grammar gets the pattern advice
mutations.expectRed: "team.>.x" is refused as no channel name before reading or sending
mutations.cell: "team.>.x" is refused as no channel name before reading or sending
mutations.note: The refusal would call team.>.x and team.** patterns and suggest posting to a channel they match, though nothing can match them.

mutations.name: N12 the refusal stops saying an offline follower may miss the post
mutations.find: A pattern follow has no durable backstop, so a follower that is offline then may miss it.
mutations.expectRed: the refusal for team.> says a pattern follow has no durable backstop
mutations.cell: the refusal for team.> says a pattern follow has no durable backstop
mutations.note: A sender who posts once and leaves would assume offline followers got it.

mutations.name: N13 a malformed name with no whole-segment wildcard is sent
mutations.expectRed: "team.**" is refused as no channel name before reading or sending
mutations.cell: "team.**" is refused as no channel name before reading or sending
mutations.note: The cold review's live defect: team.** passes the concrete check, the endpoint rewrites it to team.__, and the receipt names #team.**.

mutations.name: N14 a long name that is no channel name is shown whole
mutations.expectRed: a 65-character name that is no channel name is shown cut to its first 64 characters
mutations.cell: a 65-character name that is no channel name is shown cut to its first 64 characters
mutations.note: A name up to 4096 characters or more would be echoed whole into the refusal.

mutations.name: N15 the no-channel-name refusal drops the channel grammar
mutations.find: A channel name is segments of letters, digits, _ and - joined by dots, such as team.announce, at most
mutations.replace: A channel name is at most
mutations.expectRed: the no-channel-name refusal states the channel grammar
mutations.cell: the no-channel-name refusal states the channel grammar
mutations.note: The caller would learn the name is refused but not what a channel name is.

mutations.name: N16 the no-channel-name refusal states a limit that is not core's
mutations.find: at most ${MAX_CHANNEL_LENGTH} characters. Nothing was sent.
mutations.replace: at most 4000 characters. Nothing was sent.
mutations.expectRed: the no-channel-name refusal states core's limit of 4096 characters
mutations.cell: the no-channel-name refusal states core's limit of 4096 characters
mutations.note: A refusal that names its own number drifts from the limit core enforces.

mutations.name: N17 the cut starts one character later, so a 65-character name is shown whole
mutations.expectRed: a 65-character name that is no channel name is shown cut to its first 64 characters
mutations.cell: a 65-character name that is no channel name is shown cut to its first 64 characters
mutations.note: A name just past 64 characters would be echoed whole. A name far past the cut cannot show where it starts.

mutations.name: N18 the cut starts one character earlier, so a 64-character name gets an ellipsis
mutations.expectRed: a 64-character name that is no channel name is shown whole
mutations.cell: a 64-character name that is no channel name is shown whole

mutations.name: N19 the cut keeps the first 63 characters and the last one, losing the 64th
mutations.expectRed: a 65-character name that is no channel name is shown cut to its first 64 characters
mutations.cell: a 65-character name that is no channel name is shown cut to its first 64 characters
mutations.note: A name that repeats one character hides a cut in the wrong place, so the long names count their own positions.
